$comment: THE MOST VALUABLE FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY. If any case fails, nothing ships (SPEC 7.5). Language-neutral on purpose: the TypeScript engine consumes it now and the Kotlin port consumes it at AN2, and a divergence on any case fails both builds (D20). Never edit an expected value to make code pass - a fixture that will not pass is a question for the operator, never a code change.
source: Worked examples published by the Administration fiscale cantonale (AFC), Geneva, for the avenant of 27 June 2023 in force 1 January 2026. VERIFICATION PENDING - Checkpoint A: transcribed from SPEC-frontalier-web.md section 7.5 and not yet checked against the AFC publication itself.

commonInput.$comment: All six cases are full-time, full-year, Geneva, whole days, on the simplified 240-day basis, so totalWorkDays is 240 and fiscalCeilingDays is 96.

missionSplitNote: The published cases give a single mission total (MT). The engine takes missionDaysFrance and missionDaysThirdState separately, because France missions are imputed before third-state ones and the two are collected differently (SPEC 7.2 step 5). Every case below places the whole total in missionDaysFrance, which is the ordinary situation for a French-resident frontalier and reproduces the published Swiss/France split exactly. A case exercising the imputation ORDER is a unit test, not a fixture, since the AFC published no such example.

cases.note: Comfortably inside the ceiling. No missions, so nothing competes for the allowance and every working day is taxed in Switzerland.
Headroom binds before the cap. 96 - 91 = 5 days of room against a 10-day cap, so only 5 of the 8 mission days can be credited and 3 are taxed in France. Lands exactly on 40.00.

THE TRUNCATION CASE. The cap binds: 12 days of room but only 10 may be credited, so 94/240 = 39.1666... The AFC publishes 39.16, so the engine truncates to 2 dp. Rounding would give 39.17 and would not match the filing. This is also the case where the two rates differ most visibly - 39.16 declarable against 45.0 of days actually spent outside Switzerland.
Headroom binds hard: 2 days of room, so 2 of 12 mission days are credited and 10 are taxed in France. Lands exactly on 40.00 from the other direction to case b.

THE REGIME-LOST CASE. Telework alone (144) exceeds the ceiling (96), so the regime does not apply and mission days are EXCLUDED from the declared rate: 144/240 = 60.00, not 149/240. The missions are still taxed in France - frenchTaxedDays is 149 - which is the detail SPEC 7.2 step 5 warns is easy to get wrong. Folding them into the rate would misstate the AFC filing.

THE SECOND TRUNCATION CASE, and missions only. No telework at all, so the full 10-day cap is creditable out of 30 mission days: 10/240 = 4.1666... The AFC publishes 4.16. Proves the truncation rule is not an artefact of case c.

verificationTrace: Ruling R23. Every case carries source_url, verified_by and verified_on. They are EMPTY until the operator fills them at Checkpoint A against the primary source, and a case with empty fields is therefore VISIBLY unverified rather than silently assumed. The tests tolerate the fields and deliberately do NOT require them to be filled: making a green suite depend on verification would create pressure to fill them with something.
